findings.opportunity: validateRelationGraph already traverses every relation for duplicate, endpoint, self-loop, and ownership checks, but findCycle then traverses the complete relation array again for each of the five capability-to-capability relation types solely to rebuild per-type adjacency maps.
findings.impact: Build cycle adjacency during the existing semantic-validation pass to remove five unconditional full relation-array scans and five repeated filtering phases from every formal read, delta dry-run, sync preparation, and bootstrap gate validation; cycle detection then visits only edges of the requested type.
evidence: src/core/relations/validator.ts:22 performs the first full bundle.relations traversal.

src/core/relations/validator.ts:63 rebuilds an adjacency Map by scanning bundle.relations from the beginning on every invocation, yielding one semantic pass plus five full cycle-preparation passes.

The shared validator is called by readProjectOpsx, OPSX delta dry-run validation, change sync preparation, and bootstrap review gates, so the fixed-factor reduction applies across all required validation surfaces.
findings.recommendation: Accumulate per-type adjacency maps while validateRelationGraph performs its existing relation-order pass, then make cycle detection consume the prebuilt map instead of the full bundle.
findings.keyDesign: Create a Map keyed by each non-belongs_to RelationType whose value is an insertion-ordered Map<from, to[]>; append each eligible edge after the current semantic checks, and pass that type's adjacency map to a cycle helper that retains the existing DFS state and first-cycle policy.
preservationConstraints: Return the same { valid, errors, diagnostics } shape and preserve exact error and diagnostic ordering.
Preserve relation input order within every adjacency list and first-seen source order so the reported first cycle path remains identical.
Continue reporting only the first cycle per relation type, with precedes cycles in errors and all other non-ownership cycles in diagnostics.

Do not suppress duplicate edges, dangling endpoints, invalid endpoint kinds, or self-loops from cycle adjacency; current cycle discovery observes the raw relation list even when other semantic errors exist.
Keep ownership cardinality checks after per-relation errors and cycle messages after ownership errors.
Do not alter Registry tokens, public types, relation parsing, note policy, side effects, thrown-error timing at callers, or compatibility behavior.
implementationOutline: Initialize ordered adjacency maps for the five non-belongs_to Registry types before the relation loop.

Change findCycle to accept a prebuilt adjacency map and leave its visited, active, path, and traversal logic unchanged.
Iterate RELATION_TYPES in the current order and classify each returned cycle exactly as today.
Add an exact-order regression covering mixed duplicate, dangling, ownership, self-loop, and multiple-type cycle output.

Master began implementation after freshness check

Current src/core/relations/validator.ts accumulates insertion-ordered per-type adjacency maps during the existing relation-validation pass and passes those maps to findCycle, eliminating the five repeated full relation-array scans. Raw duplicate, dangling, invalid-endpoint, and self-loop edges remain in adjacency; relation and source order are preserved; ownership errors still precede cycle messages; and cycle classification remains unchanged. The implementation is present in commit 0ab00982 and the fresh Phase 1 reviewer recorded PASS after verifying the preservation constraints. No further actionable optimization or blocker is admitted from the current base scope.
